extraFacts.fact: API 598 covers the inspection and testing of valves, including shell, backseat and seat tests; API 609 covers butterfly valves (lug, wafer and double-flanged types, Category A and Category B); API 600 covers bolted-bonnet steel gate valves; API 602 covers compact steel gate, globe and check valves of small bore; API 603 covers corrosion-resistant bolted-bonnet gate valves; API 6D covers pipeline valves; API 594 covers wafer, lug and flanged check valves; API 599 covers metal plug valves; API 607 is the fire test for valves with non-metallic seats; BS 1868 covers steel check valves and BS 1873 steel globe valves; ASME B16.34 covers valve pressure-temperature ratings and ASME B16.10 covers valve face-to-face lengths; EN 10204 3.1 is the inspection certificate type for material certificates; ISO 15848 covers fugitive emissions of valves.

faqs.q: API 603 stainless steel gate, globe and check valve: How does API 603 differ from API 600?
faqs.a: Both are bolted-bonnet gate valves, but API 603 covers corrosion-resistant alloys with the thinner walls ASME B16.34 allows, so the valve is lighter and cheaper for the same rating. API 600 specifies heavier walls for steel valves in refinery service.

faqs.q: API 603 stainless steel gate, globe and check valve: Which stainless grade should I choose?
faqs.a: 316 (CF8M) is the general choice for chlorides and most chemicals; 304 (CF8) for milder service; the low-carbon L grades where the valve will be welded in. Duplex suits seawater and high-chloride duty. Send the fluid, concentration and temperature.

Also, standard: API 603, ASME B16.34 here, API 600, ASME B16.34 on the other. This valve is for chemical, offshore, desalination and corrosive process; the other is for oil and gas, refining, petrochemical, power, water.
